question_or_symptom: Disconnecting an admitted or issued dispatch can either leak GPU-owned storage or incorrectly retry a request that may already have rung the queue.
observation: Before a complete dispatch ACK, send timeout, cancellation, EOF, or protocol failure poisons the runtime and makes the outcome indeterminate. After a canonical ACK, wait timeout or cancellation retries the existing completion without resending. The bridge records owner disconnect phases; unissued admissions roll back, issued work quarantines packet storage until real retirement, and retired pre-wire work suppresses remaining wire records without inventing a second retirement.
conclusion: Dispatch recovery requires separate pre-admission, acknowledged-wait, and issued-work lifetimes with quarantine and exactly-once retirement semantics.
decision: Poison indeterminate pre-ACK outcomes, retry only an ACKed completion wait without allocating a new request, invalidate owner callbacks on disconnect, retain issued packet/code/kernarg storage until correlated finishPkt retirement, and suppress duplicate signal or wire completion after ownership is gone.
invalidated_assumptions: A dispatch timeout can always be retried by sending the same request again.
Freeing client-owned allocations immediately on disconnect is safe while GPU work may still be in flight.
